subject: Urgent: sudden 5xx/429 wave during morning traffic — capacity/autoscale investigation
messages:
From: Samantha Liu <samantha@finapp.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: FinApp Ops <ops@finapp.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Elevated 5xx/429s this morning — seeing timeouts and retries

Hi Marissa,

Wanted to flag a significant spike in 5xx/429 responses from the Redwood endpoint between 07:45 and 08:10 PT. Our customer-facing job queue started timing out; we observed heavy client-side retries which made the spike worse. Quick snapshot attached (metrics_snapshot_20260315.png).

Key notes from our side:
- Errors primarily 5xx (502/503) with some 429s.
- Average downstream latency for some calls jumped from ~150ms to >900ms.
- Retries from our worker fleet increased QPS by ~2.4x during the spike.

Can the team confirm whether this maps to autoscaling lag or a dedicated pool issue? This is impacting checkout flow for paying customers.

We appreciate rapid confirmation and an ETA for mitigation.

Samantha
Samantha Liu
Head of Ops, FinApp

From: dev.patel@redwood.com <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@finapp.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-15T08:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/429s this morning — seeing timeouts and retries

Samantha — thanks for the alert and the attachment. We’re pulling autoscaler and pool telemetry now. Preliminary read: a short-lived burst pushed Dedicated pool "dedicated-us-1" GPUs to >98% memory pressure around 07:48 PT; autoscaler did trigger but there was a ~90s provisioning latency for the new nodes which allowed a retry storm to amplify backend load.

Immediate actions we’ve initiated:
- Pushed a temporary burst capacity allocation to dedicated-us-1 (manual).
- Dropped the default model selection on a percentage of requests to a lower-memory variant to relieve KV cache pressure.
- Disabled aggressive client-side retries via feature-flag guidance to your SDK (we sent a small config push to ops).

I’ll follow with logs and stack traces in ~20 min. If this is blocking checkout we can also flip traffic to Hosted fallback pools (slower latency but more headroom) — confirm if acceptable.

— Dev (SE, Redwood Runtime)

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: dev.patel@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: samatha.liu@finapp.com
Date: 2026-03-15T08:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/429s this morning — capacity actions + exec notify

Looping in Rishi and Grace for visibility. Rishi — can you confirm whether the autoscaler logs show any throttling or quota events? Grace — please advise on communicating to the FinApp CS/AM team and execs; they’ll ask about SLA impacts and credits.

Also: prioritize a short one-paragraph customer-facing status and a separate technical incident note (for FinApp SRE). We should avoid overpromising but offer immediate mitigations and an RCA timeline (48–72h).

Marissa
VP, Sales & Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-15T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/429s this morning — capacity actions + exec notify

Status update from infra: autoscaler did not hit API rate limits, but we observed a control-loop oscillation. Sequence: sudden spike in short-lived long-context requests -> prolonged KV cache fills -> node oom backpressure forced worker restarts -> client retries requeued more work -> autoscaler measured CPU (not memory) and provisioned based on CPU thresholds, causing mismatch. Provisioning time for additional GPUs averaged 85–110s in that region during the event.

Concrete next steps:
1) Short term (now): keep manual burst in dedicated-us-1 and continue routing a subset of traffic to hosted fallback.
2) Near term (24–48h): tune autoscaler policy to consider GPU memory pressure / KV-cache metrics and add a fast-path for short bursts (preemptive warm standby).
3) Mitigation engineering ticket (INF-5247) opened; owner: rishi.malhotra.

I’ll attach the autoscale event log (autoscale_event_log_03-15.txt) to the incident.

-Rishi
Principal Infra Eng

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.com <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, Samantha Liu <samantha@finapp.com>
Date: 2026-03-15T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/429s this morning — customer note and exec summary

Samantha / FinApp team —

Thank you for the heads up and for the data. Brief status for your leadership: 
- What happened: a transient workload spike created GPU memory exhaustion in a Dedicated pool which, combined with short-client retries, caused a cascade of 5xx/429 for ~18 minutes.
- What we did: enabled manual burst capacity, routed a portion of traffic to hosted fallback pools, and pushed a temporary model fallback to reduce per-request GPU memory. We also advised your SDK team to reduce retry concurrency.
- Immediate impact: partial degradation of throughput for 17–20 minutes; increased latencies and elevated error rates; we estimate ~0.9% of checkout requests failed during the window.
- Next steps: RCA in 48h; infra mitigations include autoscaler policy update and warm-standby pool; we’ll propose a credits package proportionate to impacted requests.

We’ll send a short incident report within 2 business days and a technical RCA in 48–72 hours. Please let us know if you want us to open a support call with your SREs.

Best,
Grace O
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, Samantha Liu <samantha@finapp.com>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-03-15T13:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx/429s this morning — next steps and exec note

Thanks team — good triage. Sean, I’ve cc'd you to confirm whether we should route escalation to the executive incident channel for any potential SLA credit signoff. We need a crisp one-liner for the FinApp execs and an internal follow-up plan for the leadership weekly.

Action items assigned (owners):
- Rishi: INF-5247 autoscaler memory-aware policy; ETA initial spec 24h.
- Dev: post full trace logs + sample request payloads to the incident ticket; ETA 6h.
- Grace: customer-facing note + proposed credit calculation (draft) by end of day.
- Marissa: coordinate any commercial concessions / exec syncs once Grace has the figures.

Also note: please add a short appendix to the RCA with quantified retry amplification numbers and a sim of reducing retry concurrency on client side. That will help us craft guidance to customers to avoid similar cascades.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales & Customer Success
Redwood Inference
